_README: Verified tile picks, applied over the curated profiles by tools/build-mapgen-profiles.py.
The reference profiles list several 1x1 candidates per role but not which one is right, and
that is not derivable from the metadata: hasIntegratedFloorWall is one boolean per tileset
while carrying-a-floor is a per-tile property, and many sets contain both kinds. Some correct
tiles are missing from the curated lists entirely (MegaDungeon's floor-bearing wall is one).
A GUID named here is hoisted to the front of its role list, and inserted if absent, so
MapGen's 'first 1x1 candidate' rule lands on it. Setting verified:true asserts the theme has
been looked at in game on the rig — not merely that it compiles. The GUIDs are pinned rather
than left to the heuristic so that a change to the ordering rule cannot silently move a pick
that somebody has already checked.
excluded:true means the tileset provably cannot build a room: no 1x1 tile in it forms a
continuous wall face. Those themes are not offered in the UI. The reason is recorded so the
verdict can be re-argued without repeating the rig session.
Doors are a weaker claim than the structural roles. Only 3 of 20 tilesets contain a door at
all; the rest borrow one from the Doors or Doors (Modern) folder. With no pick here they all
fell back to the Dungeon door, which is the wrong look in a spaceship. The borrows follow the
reference data's own doorCompatibility list wherever it names a 1x1 tile, and the tileset's
pack where it does not. They were checked at map scale, not up close — unlike a wall, a door
cannot be mistaken for something else, so the only open question is whether it suits the set.
stairBlock is the solid cube stacked under a raised tread so a flight does not read as a row
of floating steps. Only seven sets ship one by name; Ship and Interstellar have an unnamed
full-cell solid that serves; Sewers and Shogun Palace borrow the block belonging to the set
they already borrow their stairs from. Every other theme has no such tile and the builder
fills the column with that theme's own floor instead — solid and the right material, but a
visible stack of thin slabs where the floor is thin. Those are the ones to re-curate if a
flight ever looks wrong.
Judge a tileset on a matched role set, never on one role at a time. Two sets were excluded
on evidence that turned out to be a mismatch rather than a bad tileset: Desert Village was
graded on its 2.5-tall wall/floor pieces while its plain 2.0 wall closes fine, and Chamber
was graded with a 'Chamber hold' wall standing next to a caged-tunnel corner. A wall of one
height beside a corner of another leaves a hole at every turn and reads exactly like a
tileset that cannot enclose. Swap wall, corner and cornerFiller together, then look.
Three exclusions survived that re-probe: Rural and Tavern are post-and-beam sets whose walls
genuinely do not close, and Harbor is a pier kit with no wall tile at all.

Abandoned Village.note: Solid plaster-and-beam walls; complete rooms and corridors.

Aberration.note: Fleshy combo walls, h=2.5; reads as a coherent organic dungeon.

BellowGloom.note: Combo wall h=2.5 against a curated wallHeight of 2.2 — rows are pitched off the tile, not the profile. No door compatibility is recorded for this set, so it keeps the dungeon door. The stairs pick was this set's stair *block*, so a flight was a row of stacked cubes; it is the sloped 'bg_stairs_01' now and the block moved to stairBlock where it belongs.

Brick Building.note: Solid brick walls, red interior floors.

Castle Fortified.note: Cream ashlar walls, fully enclosing. The wall is 'castle wall 1x1 base' rather than plain 'castle wall 1x1': the pack's GroupTag splits the set into a 'wall' and a 'wall base' family, the corner pick belongs to 'wall base', and the two walls are identical in size and height so nothing else distinguishes them. Reported from the rig as corners that did not match their walls. Stair pick is a merlon, which is odd but harmless. The door is 'castle door 2x2 single' — a 1x1 tile despite the name, and absent from the set's doorCompatibility list, which offers only 2x1 pieces.

CastleRuins.note: Walls are deliberately broken stubs — that is the set's intent, not a bad pick. Rooms read as ruined footprints. Shares the castle door with Castle Fortified.

Concrete Building.note: Solid concrete walls. Both corners are 2.0 and bare-shaped, so the 2.5 'concrete wall 1x1 full' combo could never be cornered without a notch at every turn; wall, corner and filler are the matched bare 2.0 set now.

Dungeon Cellar.note: Wall/Floor combo tiles, h=2.5, floor baked into wall and corner.

Facility.note: Pale panelled walls; some column and stair props look loose but the shell is solid. Flagged hasIntegratedFloorWall despite every 1x1 wall being a 1 x 0.5 panel — the set has combo *corners* but no combo wall — so the ring was seated at y=0 with no floor.

Industrial.note: Solid plated walls. Both corners are 2.0, so the 2.5 combo wall left a notch at every turn; wall and filler are the matched bare 2.0 set now. The stairs pick was this set's stair *block*, so a flight was a row of stacked cubes; it is the sloped 'industrial_stairs_01' now and the block moved to stairBlock where it belongs.

Interstellar.note: Solid tech walls; they sit low next to other sets but enclose properly.

Marble Palace.note: Solid marble walls with a chequered floor — the clearest-reading set of all. Its only 1x1 wall is a 1 x 0.5 panel, so hasIntegratedFloorWall was seating the ring at y=0 with no floor under it. doorCompatibility names only the 2x1 Palace Marble Gold, so the door falls back to the 1x1 'Door - Fancy'.

MegaDungeon.note: The 'pref' variants (h=2.5) carry a floor; plain md_wall_1x1_01 (h=2.0) does not. Neither pref tile is in the curated list, so both are inserted here. The stairs pick was this set's stair *block*, so a flight was a row of stacked cubes; it is the sloped 'md_stairs_01' now and the block moved to stairBlock where it belongs.

Sewers.note: Curated corner[0] is the 2x1 'Sewer Wall/Floor Corner'; the 1x1 '- Small' variant is the one that fits the grid. No stairs in this set, so it borrows the dungeon stair; the doors it does own are 2x1, so it takes the metal gate.

Shogun Palace.note: The whole ring is the digWall family: it is the only one in the set with a 1x1 corner. The plaster shogunPlainWall_1x1 was picked first and looks far better on its own, but its corner shogunWallCorner1x1 is 2x1 and MapGen cannot place it, so on the rig the plaster wall's white cap band ran into a bare timber block at every corner. The dig wall is 0.5 deep and authored looking west; TileEntry.AuthoredRotBias turns it, which this set is the second in-game confirmation of. No stair tile at all, so it borrows the ship's wooden stair.

Chamber.note: The matched pair 'caged tunnel lower deck wall 01' and its corner do close into a continuous face; an earlier pass paired a 'Chamber hold' wall with that corner and read the mismatch as an open cage. A cargo hold with no stair and no door of its own, so it borrows Interstellar's.

Desert Village.note: The buttressed 'Desert wall 02' closes into a continuous mudbrick face. An earlier pass judged the set on its 2.5-tall wall/floor pieces, which are narrow blocks that leave daylight between cells, and excluded it on that evidence. Wall, corner and inner corner are the matched 2.0 set. No door in the set, so it takes the Abandoned Village town door. The stairs pick was this set's stair *block*, so a flight was a row of stacked cubes; it is the sloped 'Desert Stair' now and the block moved to stairBlock where it belongs.

Harbor.note: A pier kit. The wall role resolves to 'Harbor Edge', a dock piling, and there is no enclosing piece at all.

Rural.note: Post-and-beam village set; both wall candidates come out as separated posts. Re-probed as a matched 2.0 set (Rural Wall 01 with Rural Corner and Rural Inner Corner) after that mistake was found in Desert Village, and it still leaves daylight between every post.

Tavern.note: Post-and-beam village set. 'Tavern Wall/Floor 01' is a pillar with a plank cap despite the name; every other candidate, including the Village Roof Side Walls, is the same shape. 'Tavern Wall - Small 01' and 'Tavern no floor (1x1 a)' were re-probed at 2.0 with the matching inner corner and are posts too; the set also has no 2.0 outer corner, so even a working wall would have nothing to turn with.
